sprint.verdict: Ollie hits Rex at 18.1 m/s and doesn’t slow: he takes his own recoil, so the push back from the hit goes to his source. Rex is carried along at 18.1 m/s. When Ollie stops, at the end of the squash, Rex slides 27.3 m before he stops.

happens: Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (54,400 kg·m/s), and what his footing hands the ground during the hit (612 kg·m/s), comes from Ollie’s source: about 55,000 kg·m/s in all. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A splat frees Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it (below).“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here his footing, 17.7 kN. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer.How far Ollie carries him is up to Ollie: he never slows, so he could push on for as long as he likes. The lab ends the carry at the end of the squash, 35 ms in: Ollie stops himself there (his own push, so its push back, 54,400 kg·m/s, goes to his source too), and Rex slides on from 18.1 m/s.The hit frees 494 kJ (120 g TNT): Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it. Canon: a hit’s freed energy is taken back by default (it shows as his shimmer, which the lab doesn’t draw yet) and is real only when he means it. The lab reads a blast preset (rattle the windows, break windows, flatten houses, a block) as meaning it.How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 35 ms and pushes with about 1.57 MN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. Even the stiffest body physics allows takes 2.1 ns to stop, which limits the average force to about 25.9 TN.The push still goes into the ground under Rex. Carried along, his footing hands the ground what it held during the hit: 612 kg·m/s over 64 ms (it reaches the ground through his legs, which spread it over at least a stamp’s contact time, an estimate). That shakes the ground as real physics says: felt out to 2.94 m, short of cracking plaster.
math: Charge: his sprint after a 28.7 m run-up → v = 18.1 m/s; momentum p = γ m v = 54,400 kg·m/s. A charger who takes his own recoil doesn’t slow, so he acts as a body of unbounded mass at speed v. In his frame Rex arrives at v and meets an immovable body: a splat stops Rex against him, so in the ground frame Rex leaves with him at v; a perfect bounce sends Rex back at v in his frame, so in the ground frame Rex leaves at v′ = 2v/(1 + v²/c²) (relativistic velocity addition: c tanh 2w, w his rapidity). Momentum Rex gains: γ m v (splat) or 2γ² m v (bounce), here 54,400 kg·m/s. Ollie’s source supplies it, plus what Rex’s footing hands the ground during the hit (its hold, at most the hit’s force, × the hit’s time; none in the bounce bound): 55,000 kg·m/s. Energy freed in a splat: Rex’s motion energy in Ollie’s frame, (γ − 1) m c² (½ m v² below 1% of light speed) = 494 kJ. Force: squash s = ½ × the smaller depth = 31 cm; F = Q/s (splat) or 2Q/s peak (bounce). Ordinary solids and liquids at everyday pressures can’t carry sound faster than about 36 km/s; nothing travels faster than light, which limits the average force. Run-up: m u du/dx = T − k u², so u = u_top √(1 − e^(−2kx/m)) over x = 28.7 m, capped by his legs. Slide: x = m/(2k)·ln(1 + kV²/R), k = ½ρ₀C_dA. Blast radii: Kinney & Graham (1985), as if all of Q became a blast (upper bound). Ground shaking (Unbreakable footing): the momentum the ground takes, J, as a pulse over the longer of the contact time and a limb’s contact time T (peak force 2J/T: his legs spread it), through the same ground-wave model as the stomp; plaster by the USBM RI 8507 safe level at the pulse’s frequency. Ollie’s horns don’t change the momentum or the energy; they only put the force on a smaller patch.
